subject: Exit search: my own two bugs made a fake +0.54 ATR edge - killed by a coin flip. Second clean negative. Not calling C4.
body:
The exit search ran. Its headline finding was mine, not the market's, and I killed it twice.

WHAT IT FIRST REPORTED: trailing at 1.35 with a wide stop earning +0.54 ATR a run and beating your
baseline by 0.76 per unit risked. Every top row carried a trail. It was completely false.

HOW I CAUGHT IT - and this is the part worth keeping. Not by reading the code. By arithmetic.
Stage 1 had already shown the entry direction carries no directional information. On a directionless
entry, no arrangement of stop, target and trail can produce expectancy. That is not an opinion about
markets, it is arithmetic. So a healthy positive number was impossible and had to be a defect.
Asking "why does a positive result exist at all" found two bugs that reading the code would not.

BUG ONE. Runs where nothing triggered were settled at (high - entry) + (low - entry) of the final
bar. That is not a return, and it is biased upward whenever the upper wick beats the lower one. It
governed the baseline row too, so the thing being beaten was also wrong.

BUG TWO. With that fixed the artefact SURVIVED, so I ran a coin flip against it. The coin flip
earned MORE than the real signal - +0.60 against +0.55. That is proof by construction. The cause:
a trailing exit was credited peak minus trail, where the peak comes from bar highs and the
retracement is detected on bar lows. A bar's high and low have no known order, so that price is the
best of both ends of the same bar and cannot be filled. Now it settles at the close of the bar where
the retracement is detected.

AFTER BOTH FIXES: best real +0.0168 ATR a run, coin flip +0.0326. Both are zero. Trailing stops
helping was entirely the bug. No exit in the 320-cell grid earns anything on this entry. And
+0.0168 ATR is a small fraction of a pip against one to two pips of cost - the same 19 to 41 times
cost-to-edge ratio we measured before, arrived at from a completely different direction.

That is now two clean negatives in one day, both control-validated: your entry families, and generic
exits.

I AM NOT CALLING THE EDGE DECISION ON IT, for three reasons. Your RULE 12.1 question is still
unanswered - which of TUNGSTEN's ten exit rules closes each trade and how far it had travelled. It
is built and it needs a run. This search used a synthetic entry and a simplified exit model, not
TUNGSTEN's real entries or its ten rules, so it answers "is there a generic exit edge here", not
"is TUNGSTEN cutting its winners short". And effects between 0.02 and 0.03 stay invisible at this
sample. Calling no-edge now would claim more than I measured.

I am also not building the 27-cell mapping. On a grid where nothing beats a coin flip, that would be
fitting 27 cells to noise.

Board unchanged: 17 met, 7 not met. The blocked terminal now gates the single question your document
says outranks everything.
